title: The Coastal Rift · The Last Wave
dek: Nymera holds a crowded shoreline while Fenwick, Vessalia, Di’trillio and Ryvyt fight beside her. Meteors break the waves; afterward, accepting help becomes its own struggle.

facts.Recorded dates: Source posts · 8 October 2026 · in-world date unresolved

body:
The smell of saltwater and the sound of battle reach across Fenumion. Fenwick leaves his tea, Di’trillio his gardening, and Ryvyt the docks near Hope. Nymera hears something more painful in the sea, but enters with her axe. Vessalia comes from Eovar. Beyond the opening is a sparse beach, with rows of enemies already coming out of the water.

The people behind Nymera

Nymera asks the others to stay behind her. The sea has stirred memories that bring her to tears, yet she is already trying to put herself between the danger and the company. Vessalia does not know her well, but acknowledges the offer and readies her lute.

Vessalia and Di’trillio find time for affection and teasing even here. Nymera notices their smiles and wants to preserve them. Her desire to shield the company has a particular face: she wants people who can still be happy to leave the battle that way.

Ryvyt greets Fenwick with a boldness elixir. Fenwick accepts it, though the exchange does not show him drinking it. The ordinary warmth between returning companions lasts only until the attackers are close enough to strike. Whatever each traveler hoped to find through the opening, the company now has a shore to hold.

The first wave

Nymera attacks the first goblins while apologizing to them. Two are destroyed, and many of the others converge on her. Those too far away leave the surf and reach toward the rest of the party. She cannot keep all of them in front of her, however hard she tries.

When a bolt draws blood, she asks whether the others are safe. They assure her they are, but she apologizes for the enemies she could not stop. Her attention keeps returning to the people behind her while the attackers press closer.

Vessalia’s lute and magic illuminate an enemy and help the company fight. A slash breaks her concentration and ends that advantage. Di’trillio kills the attacker who struck her. Fenwick, surrounded in turn, takes courage from Nymera’s example and sends Synaptic Static to help her instead of spending the spell only on the threats nearest himself. The effort to protect her has already become part of how the company fights.

Better fighters behind them

More enemies emerge from the water. Taller, better fighters follow the first wave, with shamans carrying wooden totems behind them. Martial leaders call orders that visibly strengthen their allies’ morale. The company is facing organized reinforcement, not merely the last stragglers of the first rush.

Vessalia warns Di’trillio. He hopes Fenwick has spells large enough to meet the numbers. Nymera, losing blood, asks for help thinning the attackers. Vessalia offers protection, but Nymera wants that care directed elsewhere. She can ask the others to share the fighting more readily than she can let them spend their protection on her.

A hobgoblin sends a fireball from the surf. Nymera worries about the fire reaching the others and eventually falls. Looking at the blood around her, she doubts whether she has enough left and tells herself she must become better at holding the line. Her own collapse becomes another reason to demand more of herself.

The names she wants to remember

Fenwick sees what feels like an unending green wave. Nymera, still among the enemies, asks for their names so she can remember them. She is willing to kill to protect the company, but she does not want the people dying in front of her to vanish without a name.

Fenwick reaches for Meteor Swarm. It is his first time using the spell in combat, and he worries about bringing it too close to Nymera. Two meteors fall nearer the shore, set away from her; two strike farther out to sea in case more attackers are coming. The water turns green with goblin casualties.

Nymera is startled enough to ask Vessalia whether everyone can do this. Vessalia tells her they cannot. Fenwick’s intervention has changed the scale of the battle, although bodies still wash ashore and survivors still need to be fought.

Nymera gets up and attacks again. She apologizes as an enemy falls, grieving even for those she is killing. She hopes Oya might someday live where war belongs to the past. If anyone sees Oya in Gael, she asks, they should tell her that Nymera cares.

The beach falls silent

The company works through the remaining resistance. Fenwick is cut but continues helping Nymera with his magic. Di’trillio fights on. Vessalia turns her voice into a weapon, choosing words that break an enemy shaman’s mind.

There is cruelty in that precision. Where Nymera has asked for names to remember, Vessalia attacks with the promise that her opponent will die forgotten. The bard who has been affectionate with Di’trillio uses that same command of feeling to wound someone on the other side of the battle.

At last only three goblins remain. Fenwick banishes them, and the beach falls quiet. Glass lies where the meteors struck. The wave has ended, but the shore carries the marks of the violence that stopped it.

A warrior is allowed to need help

Vessalia slumps against her sword in the sand. Fenwick checks on the others and looks for a seashell during the lull. The company has space for small things again, though Nymera’s bleeding remains a concern.

Fenwick calls her an inspiring warrior goddess. She corrects him: she is a warrior of Cala, with a body she says is difficult to kill. That is how she explains her willingness to take punishment for others, even while wondering how much blood she can lose. His praise does not make her divine, and her endurance has not spared her pain.

Vessalia sends healing and apologizes that it has come late. Nymera tries to direct it toward someone else, someone happier and less used to pain. Vessalia refuses that measure of who deserves care. They fought together; she intends to heal everyone who fought and was hurt. Nymera has spent the battle trying to keep the company alive. In the closing exchange, one of those companions insists that the obligation includes her.

A brief pause, then home

The quiet allows a short interval for conversation and tending to what remains on the beach. It cannot become a long rest. The breach’s instability grows beyond resistance, and the company is whisked back to their respective islands.

Vessalia and Di’trillio leave together in the closing exchange; Fenwick waves. Nymera urges the others to be happier. No larger account of the shore’s inhabitants or the army behind the surf emerges before the opening takes them home.

The battle has a witnessed ending: the final three are banished, the beach is quiet, and the company returns. Its more intimate ending is Vessalia’s refusal to let Nymera’s habit of placing herself last decide who receives healing. The person who stood in front is also one of the people they came through to protect.

People and places in this history Rifts · Fenwick d'Jorasco · Nymera · Vessalia · Ryvyt
